title: Arias with a Twist by Joey Arias and Basil Twist at the HERE Arts Cen...
transcript: I often lament how I missed out on some of the golden ages of downtown New York performance and old school drag. And although it's only 20ish years old, Arias with a Twist somewhat pacifies this itch with its off-beat panache and its scrappy production elements. It premiered in New York in 2008, toured internationally, and is now returning to its original home as a beloved theatrical fantasia, cabaret drag performance, and puppet show. Aided by numerous puppeteers and a band of marionettes, Joey Arias endures an alien abduction followed by a wild journey through various locations of infamy such as the jungle, which I interpreted as Eden, Hell, and of course, New York City. I had no idea where this was going, and I'm not quite sure what to make of Joey's assured but often disoriented persona, but I was consistently absorbed by Joey's distinctive vocal style and the charmingly rugged production elements. It's a trippy experience, and the way that the projections and puppetry blend into the scenic design and play with scale give it an immersive quality that's hard to achieve with a live performance. I also appreciated how practical the effects are and how it's clear that the goal of this production isn't to 2026-ify a 2008 show. There's a beauty in archiving something by reintroducing it to new audiences more or less exactly as it was. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses genuine appreciation for the production's vocal style, puppetry, and preserved aesthetic, though with some ambivalence about Joey's persona and narrative clarity. Overall tone is enthusiastic but measured.
